title: Psalms Chapter 71 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 71 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 71 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 71.

questions.question: In Psalms 71, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Let my mouth be filled with thy praise
questions.explanation: The phrase 'In thee, O LORD, do I put my trust' appears first in Psalms 71:1.

questions.question: What does the psalmist ask the LORD to do in Psalms 71:2?
questions.explanation: The psalmist asks for deliverance, inclining of the ear, and salvation in Psalms 71:2.

questions.question: According to Psalms 71:3, what is the psalmist's strong habitation?
questions.explanation: The psalmist refers to the LORD as his strong habitation in Psalms 71:3.

questions.question: Who does the psalmist seek deliverance from in Psalms 71:4?
questions.explanation: The psalmist seeks deliverance from the wicked and the unrighteous and cruel man in Psalms 71:4.

questions.question: What has the psalmist recognized about the LORD since his youth according to Psalms 71:5?
questions.explanation: The psalmist declares the LORD as his hope in Psalms 71:5.

questions.question: From where has the LORD held up the psalmist according to Psalms 71:6?
questions.explanation: The psalmist states he has been held up from the womb in Psalms 71:6.

questions.question: What does the psalmist say he is to many in Psalms 71:7?
questions.explanation: The psalmist describes himself as a wonder unto many in Psalms 71:7.

questions.question: What does the psalmist want his mouth to be filled with in Psalms 71:8?
questions.explanation: The psalmist desires his mouth to be filled with praise and honour in Psalms 71:8.

questions.question: The psalmist expresses trust in the LORD in which verse?
questions.explanation: The psalmist puts his trust in the LORD in Psalms 71:1.

questions.question: In Psalms 71:4, who does the psalmist refer to as 'my God'?
questions.explanation: The psalmist refers to the LORD as 'my God' in Psalms 71:4.

questions.question: What does the psalmist ask for in Psalms 71:2?
questions.explanation: The psalmist specifically asks to escape in Psalms 71:2.

questions.question: True or False: The psalmist claims his praise shall be continually of the LORD.
questions.explanation: The psalmist states his praise shall be continually of the LORD in Psalms 71:6.

questions.question: True or False: The psalmist mentions being filled with despair in Psalms 71.
questions.explanation: The psalmist does not mention despair; he speaks of trust and praise.

questions.question: True or False: The psalmist asks to be delivered from the hands of the righteous.
questions.explanation: The psalmist specifically asks for deliverance from the wicked and unrighteous, not the righteous, in Psalms 71:4.

questions.question: True or False: The psalmist describes the LORD as his strong refuge.
questions.explanation: The psalmist describes himself as a wonder and the LORD as his strong refuge, not the other way around in Psalms 71:7.

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 71 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 71 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What does the psalmist request in Psalms 71:9?
options: Cast me off in the time of old age
Forsake me not when my strength faileth
questions.correctAnswer: Forsake me not when my strength faileth
questions.explanation: The psalmist requests God not to forsake him as he ages and his strength diminishes, as stated in Psalms 71:9.

questions.question: What does Psalms 71:3 promise will happen if someone trusts the Lord as their strong habitation?
options: They will be put to confusion
They will continually resort to Him
They will escape from the wicked
questions.correctAnswer: They will continually resort to Him
questions.explanation: Psalms 71:3 indicates that trusting the Lord as a strong habitation leads to continual reliance on Him.

questions.question: Who does the psalmist say is speaking against him in Psalms 71:10?
questions.explanation: Psalms 71:10 clearly states that the psalmist's enemies are speaking against him.

questions.question: What do the adversaries of the psalmist seek to do according to Psalms 71:13?
questions.explanation: Psalms 71:13 indicates that the adversaries are seeking to confound and consume the psalmist.

questions.question: According to Psalms 71:14, what will the psalmist do continually?
questions.explanation: Psalms 71:14 expresses the psalmist's commitment to continually praise God.

questions.question: What does Psalms 71:15 say the psalmist will show forth all the day?
questions.explanation: The psalmist declares in Psalms 71:15 that he will show forth God's righteousness and salvation throughout the day.

questions.question: In Psalms 71:16, what does the psalmist say he will go in?
options: The strength of the Lord GOD
questions.correctAnswer: The strength of the Lord GOD
questions.explanation: The psalmist states in Psalms 71:16 that he will go in the strength of the Lord God.

questions.question: What is the psalmist's plea in Psalms 71:12?
options: For God to be far from him
For God to make haste for help
questions.correctAnswer: For God to make haste for help
questions.explanation: Psalms 71:12 expresses the psalmist's urgent plea for God's immediate help.

questions.question: What does Psalms 71:11 indicate about the psalmist's enemies?
options: They believe God has forsaken him
questions.correctAnswer: They believe God has forsaken him
questions.explanation: Psalms 71:11 reveals that the psalmist's enemies are claiming that God has forsaken him.

questions.question: According to Psalms 71:5, what has the psalmist made God since his youth?
questions.explanation: Psalms 71:5 indicates that the psalmist has made God his hope from his youth.

questions.question: What might the psalmist's trust in God lead to according to Psalms 71:2?
questions.explanation: Psalms 71:2 highlights that trusting in God leads to deliverance through His righteousness.

questions.question: What does the psalmist ask God to be in Psalms 71:1?
questions.explanation: Psalms 71:1 states that the psalmist puts his trust in the Lord.

questions.question: True or False: The psalmist asks God to cast him off in old age.
questions.explanation: The psalmist actually asks God not to cast him off, as stated in Psalms 71:9.

questions.question: True or False: The psalmist is confident that God will not forsake him.
questions.explanation: The psalmist expresses confidence in God's support and help throughout the psalm, particularly in Psalms 71:14.

questions.question: True or False: The psalmist desires to silence the praises of God.
questions.explanation: The psalmist expresses a desire to continually praise God, as shown in Psalms 71:14.

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 71 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 71.

questions.question: What has God taught the psalmist from his youth?
questions.explanation: This is confirmed in Psalms 71:17 where the psalmist states, 'O God, thou hast taught me from my youth: and hitherto have I declared thy wondrous works.'

questions.question: What does the psalmist ask God not to do as he becomes old and grayheaded?
questions.explanation: The psalmist pleads in Psalms 71:18, 'Now also when I am old and grayheaded, O God, forsake me not...'

questions.question: In Psalms 71:19, what attribute of God is described as very high?
questions.explanation: Psalms 71:19 states, 'Thy righteousness also, O God, is very high...'

questions.question: What does the psalmist believe God will do after showing him great troubles?
questions.explanation: According to Psalms 71:20, 'Thou, which hast shewed me great and sore troubles, shalt quicken me again...'

questions.question: What musical instruments does the psalmist say he will use to praise God?
questions.explanation: In Psalms 71:22, the psalmist declares, 'I will also praise thee with the psaltery, even thy truth, O my God: unto thee will I sing with the harp...'

questions.question: What does the psalmist claim he will talk about all day long?
questions.explanation: Psalms 71:24 states, 'My tongue also shall talk of thy righteousness all the day long...'

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'תָּמִיד' (tamid) in Psalms 71:14 mean?
questions.explanation: 'תָּמִיד' (tamid) translates to 'always' and reflects the psalmist's continual hope and praise.

questions.question: Which literary technique is used in Psalms 71:18 regarding the psalmist's age?
questions.explanation: Psalms 71:18 uses parallelism in expressing the psalmist's plea to be sustained in old age and to show God's strength.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the theme of God’s righteousness as seen in Psalms 71:19?
questions.explanation: Romans 1:17 echoes the theme of God's righteousness: 'For therein is the righteousness of God revealed from faith to faith: as it is written, The just shall live by faith.'

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the theme of hope in Psalms 71:14?
questions.explanation: Romans 15:13 relates to hope, stating, 'Now the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, that ye may abound in hope, through the power of the Holy Ghost.'

questions.question: What comes before Psalms 71:17?
questions.explanation: Psalms 71:16 precedes 17, stating, 'I will go in the strength of the Lord GOD...'

questions.question: What comes after Psalms 71:21?
questions.explanation: Psalms 71:22 follows 21, where the psalmist continues to express praise with musical instruments.

questions.question: Psalms 71:20 speaks of God bringing the psalmist up from what?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'Thou, which hast shewed me great and sore troubles, shalt quicken me again, and shalt bring me up again from the depths of the earth.' (Psalms 71:20)

questions.question: The psalmist believes his enemies will be what?
questions.explanation: The psalmist expresses hope that those who seek his hurt will be confounded and brought to shame (Psalms 71:24).

questions.question: The psalmist declares he will never forget God's mercy.
questions.explanation: While the psalmist expresses trust and praise, there is no specific declaration of never forgetting God's mercy in this chapter.

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 71 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 71 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Psalms 71:5 teach about God's nature in relation to the believer's life?
options: God is the believer's hope and trust from youth
God is indifferent to human suffering
God's justice is delayed until the end of time
God only saves in moments of crisis
questions.correctAnswer: God is the believer's hope and trust from youth
questions.explanation: Psalms 71:5 states, 'For thou art my hope, O Lord GOD: thou art my trust from my youth,' highlighting God's enduring role as the believer's hope and trust throughout life.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning salvation is taught in Psalms 71:20?
options: God revives and restores the believer from the depths of despair
Salvation is only for the righteous in their prime
God does not intervene in human suffering
Salvation depends on human effort alone
questions.correctAnswer: God revives and restores the believer from the depths of despair
questions.explanation: Psalms 71:20 says, 'Thou, which hast shewed me great and sore troubles, shalt quicken me again, and shalt bring me up again from the depths of the earth,' teaching that God actively revives and restores His people even after severe trials.

questions.question: What doctrine about sanctification is indicated in Psalms 71:17?
options: God teaches the believer from youth leading to continual declaration of His works
Sanctification is a one-time event only
Believers are sanctified through human wisdom alone
questions.correctAnswer: God teaches the believer from youth leading to continual declaration of His works
questions.explanation: Psalms 71:17 states, 'O God, thou hast taught me from my youth: and hitherto have I declared thy wondrous works,' emphasizing sanctification as a lifelong process of divine teaching and testimony.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Psalms 71:3 specifically demonstrate?
options: God as a fortress and rock demonstrating covenant faithfulness
God's omniscience in knowing all events
questions.correctAnswer: God as a fortress and rock demonstrating covenant faithfulness
questions.explanation: Verse 3 describes God as 'my rock and my fortress,' indicating His steadfastness and faithfulness in covenant protection for the believer.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted in Psalms 71:9 with the plea 'Cast me not off in the time of old age'?
questions.explanation: Psalms 71:9 pleads, 'Cast me not off in the time of old age; forsake me not when my strength faileth,' emphasizing God's enduring loyalty and steadfastness even in the believer's weakness.

questions.question: How does Psalms 71:18 connect to the broader redemptive-historical theme of legacy and witness?
options: It expresses the importance of declaring God's strength to future generations
It focuses exclusively on past personal salvation
It denies any role of older believers in teaching youth
It suggests salvation is only individual and not communal
questions.correctAnswer: It expresses the importance of declaring God's strength to future generations
questions.explanation: Verse 18 says, '...until I have shewed thy strength unto this generation, and thy power to every one that is to come,' highlighting the biblical theme of passing down faith through generations.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection is found in Psalms 71:22 regarding worship and God's truth?
options: It anticipates New Testament praise of God through music and truth
It limits worship to silent meditation only
It discourages singing as a form of worship
It emphasizes ritual over heartfelt praise
questions.correctAnswer: It anticipates New Testament praise of God through music and truth
questions.explanation: Verse 22 states, 'I will also praise thee with the psaltery, even thy truth, O my God,' connecting Old Testament worship with the New Testament practice of praising God through music and truth.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Psalms 71:6 and 71:17 teach about divine providence and instruction?
options: God sustains and instructs the believer from birth throughout life
God only intervenes sporadically with no continuous care
Instruction from God is irrelevant to salvation
questions.correctAnswer: God sustains and instructs the believer from birth throughout life
questions.explanation: Verse 6 speaks of God holding the psalmist from the womb, and verse 17 speaks of teaching from youth onward, together teaching God's ongoing providence and instruction.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Psalms 71:14 and 71:15 teach about hope and proclamation in the Christian life?
options: Continuing hope leads to unceasing praise and proclamation of God's salvation
Hope is passive and does not result in praise
Proclamation is only for clergy, not all believers
questions.correctAnswer: Continuing hope leads to unceasing praise and proclamation of God's salvation
questions.explanation: Verse 14 promises continual hope and increasing praise, and verse 15 commits to proclaiming God's righteousness and salvation all day, linking hope to active proclamation.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about divine justice and human opposition is taught in Psalms 71:10 and 71:13?
options: God will confound and consume adversaries who plot against the believer
Human enemies are victorious over God's people
God ignores the counsel of the wicked
Divine justice delays indefinitely, allowing evil to triumph
questions.correctAnswer: God will confound and consume adversaries who plot against the believer
questions.explanation: Verse 10 describes enemies plotting harm, and verse 13 petitions God to confound and consume those adversaries, teaching assured divine justice against opposition.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Psalms 71:9-12 teaches that God abandons the aged and weak. What does Psalms 71:9-12 actually teach?
options: The psalmist pleads for God's presence and help despite enemies claiming God has forsaken him
The psalmist agrees that God has abandoned him
God is indifferent to human suffering and aging
The passage shows that faith fails in old age
questions.correctAnswer: The psalmist pleads for God's presence and help despite enemies claiming God has forsaken him
questions.explanation: Verses 9-12 show the psalmist asking God not to forsake him in old age while enemies falsely claim God has abandoned him, demonstrating trust rather than abandonment.

questions.question: What doctrine does Psalms 71:24 teach about the believer's response to persecution?
options: The believer continuously speaks of God's righteousness despite being shamed by enemies
The believer should hide and avoid speaking about God under persecution
Silence is the only proper response to opposition
questions.correctAnswer: The believer continuously speaks of God's righteousness despite being shamed by enemies
questions.explanation: Verse 24 states the tongue will talk of God's righteousness all day long even as enemies are confounded, teaching perseverance in witness under persecution.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is demonstrated in Psalms 71:21 where God is said to 'comfort me on every side'?
questions.explanation: Verse 21 expresses that God comforts on every side, indicating His omnipresent care and compassionate presence with the believer.

questions.question: What theological synthesis is found between Psalms 71:1 and Psalms 71:12 regarding trust and divine help?
options: Trust in God is foundational, yet the believer actively pleads for God's timely help
Divine help is only given without human petition
Trust in God excludes requests for deliverance
questions.correctAnswer: Trust in God is foundational, yet the believer actively pleads for God's timely help
questions.explanation: Verse 1 declares trust in God, and verse 12 urgently asks God to make haste to help, showing trust accompanied by earnest petition.

questions.question: How does Psalms 71:7 contribute to the doctrine of God as refuge amid human perception?
options: Although others wonder at the psalmist, God remains his strong refuge
God is distant and uncaring about human wonder
The psalmist is isolated without divine protection
Human opinion is more reliable than God's protection
questions.correctAnswer: Although others wonder at the psalmist, God remains his strong refuge
questions.explanation: Verse 7 says, 'I am as a wonder unto many; but thou art my strong refuge,' showing God's protective role despite human skepticism.
